title: רב אחא מבי חוזאה

paragraphs: Rav Acha of Bei Chozai. Chana bar Issi brought Acha [אחא, which can also mean ‘a brother’] from Bei Chozai, chapter Hamafkid. (Siftei Yeshenim, Sha'ar Bat Rabbim, understood likewise.) Brother, see his error: Hamafkid 39b and Ketubbot 27b have a man from Bei Chozai come to Mari bar Isak, claiming to be his brother and seeking a share of their father’s property. He understood this as a sage’s name, Rav Acha of Chozai. But he forgot Gittin 7a: “Tziklag, Madmannah, and Sansannah”—Rav Acha of Bei Chozai said that when a person has a complaint against his neighbor concerning sustenance and remains silent, the One dwelling in the bush judges for him. There he appears to be in Rav Ashi’s time.
